answer: A practical anti-Sybil design charges an escalating price for each extra identity one operator creates. The first identity is nearly free, like a zephyr passing unnoticed, but the second, third and tenth each demand a steeper fee and a heavier proof-of-work task. At the vertex of this curve, running a thousand fake agents costs far more than any reward they could harvest. A small delta in cost between identity one and two is harmless, yet compounded across hundreds of identities it bankrupts the attacker while honest users, who need only one identity, barely notice.
